Sample dispositions and rule review — 2026-10-21

f5b95b44a68582a7ff38b9e51786fc9f50d137d910d3b48b618a49dbac96847b.exe
Identification: Softonic_DLM / Softonic_2 download manager for TreeSize.
Verdict: MALICIOUS (potentially unwanted offer-bundle downloader).

The PE is an Inno Setup 6.7.0 Delphi loader. osslsigncode verified its
Authenticode digest, signature, timestamp, chain and CRLs. Signer:
SOFTONIC INTERNATIONAL SA. Signed 2026-09-09. The nonstandard checksum is
not evidence of a broken signature. GETUFID explicitly uses the PE checksum
as a fallback download/configuration identifier when the executable filename
has no suitable identifier; this explains its use as an application field.

The installed innoextract 1.9 cannot parse this version. A locally built
upstream pull-request branch (dscho/innoextract, inno-6.4-to-6.7-support)
parsed it and recovered four UI image/icon files. Instrumenting the parser
also recovered 173718 bytes of compiled PascalScript. Binary Refinery IFPS
disassembly was used to trace the script, rather than inferring behavior
from the loader's imports or compression entropy.

InitializeSetup sets Softonic/Softonic_DLM/Softonic_2. GETREMOTEJSON creates
WinHttp.WinHttpRequest.5.1 and POSTs GETREQUESTPOSTDATA to the configured
CloudFront /o endpoint. INITMAINCARRIER obtains its title, URL, filename and
arguments from the returned i object. INITPRODS parses the o offer array,
including display information, download paths, command arguments, architecture,
installed-app, registry, process, browser, disk/RAM, geography and recent
antivirus-uninstall eligibility checks. These checks serve offer targeting;
they do not establish sandbox evasion or antivirus disabling.

SHOWDNLDPAGE -> DNLDFILE downloads the carrier and selected offer files.
TDownloadWizardPage.Add receives an empty required SHA256 string. INSTALLPRODS
checks file magic, renames ZIP/EXE content, extracts ZIPs, locates an executable
and calls ShellExec using remotely supplied command arguments. Offer pages and
checked/unchecked selection state are present. SENDREPORT includes installer,
user/session identifiers, OS/architecture, campaign and installation events;
GETUSERID reads MachineGuid, and GETSLACKHIVE inventories Slack registry keys.
This is tracking and installed-software inventory in a commercial bundle;
no credentials, document theft, injected payload or persistence was established.

Read-only configuration retrieval was reproduced using synthetic OS/language
values and the artifact's checksum identifier 1816926106. The exact configuration
identified TreeSize 9.8.1 as the requested carrier and returned five offers.
A generic request returned six offers: Avast One, Opera, AVG Anti Virus,
Avast Secure Browser, CCleaner and Avast VPN. Commands include /silent and
--silent with advertising/campaign parameters. One offer ZIP was retrieved;
its executable has a verified Gen Digital Inc. signature. The TreeSize carrier
URL returned HTTP 412, so its current bytes could not be analyzed. No installer
was executed. The landing-page consent flow, original download circumstances,
user selections and historical server responses remain unknown.

The observed advertising offer distribution, remote installer control and
silent partner installation, together with the supplied PUA provenance, tip
the security-engineer disposition toward quarantine as unwanted software.
This does not assert that TreeSize, Avast, Opera or the signer is malware.

One independent suspicious family profile is supported on the outer PE and
was added under well-known/unwanted/offercore. It requires Softonic product
metadata, the signer, Inno foundation and a payload-sized overlay. The
requested two hostile/two suspicious minimum cannot be honestly met from the
outer PE's currently extracted facts: the substantive script is compressed
and unsupported by the installed extractor. A second redundant identity rule
or a hostile label on ordinary installer compression would invent evidence.
No such rule was added. Neutral execution/crypto/privilege traits remain.

bootstrap.js — b5de8fd50518000158e7e3fae41b48cfe58582ecfccb1b53b9ade9e7224c2237
Identification: unmodified Bootstrap 4.6.0 UMD distribution.
Verdict: BENIGN.

The complete 144033-byte file exactly matches the official release:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/twbs/bootstrap/v4.6.0/dist/js/bootstrap.js
The UMD entrypoint imports jquery/popper.js or uses existing browser globals.
Its exports are normal UI widgets. Timers drive transitions, carousels and
toasts; input handlers toggle/focus UI controls. Tooltip HTML follows the
sanitizer allowlist/URL checks. No hidden appendage, decoded payload, remote
fetch, cookie harvesting, OS execution or exfiltration was found. URLs are
license/docs/error references. Representative declared peer releases jquery
3.5.1 and popper.js 1.16.1 were fetched and inspected. The sample does not pin
which peer versions a deploying site used. No malicious dependency was found.
Possible collection reasons include an old UI library collected from a hostile
web page or heuristic matches on DOM manipulation and computed dispatch;
the external source's exact rationale is unavailable.

superadminx-admin-v4.1.5.zip
5416c8d857ef2f03594ca54b9a44b55877447d4e7d4d7dc8234d9e89fac21fa0
Identification: SuperAdminx v4.1.5 Webman/PHP + React administration framework,
with a nested uni-app client and vendored libraries.
Verdict: BENIGN.

All 855 non-directory archive members match the upstream v4.1.5 GitHub archive
byte for byte, including the nested ZIP. The tag resolves to commit
065b2f9ef8870ea8503606d85b034679ac666a3a:
https://api.github.com/repos/zouyi741599086/SuperAdminx/git/ref/tags/v4.1.5
https://api.github.com/repos/zouyi741599086/SuperAdminx/zipball/v4.1.5
TinyMCE core and silver theme exactly match npm tinymce 8.3.2. Both ECharts
bundles exactly match npm echarts 6.0.0, not the initially checked 5.3.3.

Webman startup and middleware route admin/API requests through JWT checks.
JwtAdmin loads the active administrator and checks role/menu permissions;
controller onLogin flags and per-method exemptions determine authentication.
GeneratorFileLogic restricts writing generated backend/frontend source to
app.debug. File upload code checks extension, MIME and size; remote image
fetch checks MIME and writes image bytes. TLS peer verification is disabled
in an image downloader (accurate notable finding retained). Windows taskkill
terminates development worker PIDs, and Monitor's exec runs PHP lint during
source monitoring. AES/RSA/base64 support encrypts application API traffic;
it is not a hidden execution chain. The frontend API base is deployment
configuration; the nested sample client points to shop.superadminx.com.
That endpoint had an expired TLS certificate and, when retrieved without
certificate verification for inspection, returned a site-suspended page.
No downloaded executable script was found at that endpoint.

Inspected dependency tarballs/source include unusual declared install/new/to,
vite-plugin-javascript-obfuscator, esbuild/fsevents lifecycle-bearing entries,
superadminx/think_validate and webman-framework, plus the published UI/crypto
libraries. The new package is an old Initializr CLI with a curl/unzip/git
workflow, not an install hook used by this project. The Vite plugin applies
the configured source obfuscator at build time. jsencrypt's eval strings are
webpack development modules implementing RSA/ASN.1; they are not a fetched
payload. The source includes ordinary build-time debug/self-defending options.
An upstream match and this bounded dependency review do not establish safety
of every future dependency resolution or of an arbitrary deployed instance.

The source's exact malware-label rationale is unknown. Plausible triggers
are the bundled minified/eval-based libraries, encryption code and code-writing
administration tooling. Specific incorrect findings were verified against code:
TinyMCE toolbar shell:true does not spawn a shell; DOM unlink is not fs.unlink;
Pinia detached:true detaches a subscription; scaleToFill is an image mode;
model_code is ORM source; a standalone write method proves no filesystem sink;
sha256 text near split/concat does not prove a next-stage address.

Rule changes and verification

Added the Softonic signed Inno download-manager identity profile. Tightened
launch-option rules to process launch call expressions and repeated unlink to
fs.unlink calls. Tightened the ToFil shard to a complete literal. Removed
unbound write-method filesystem inference and kept Scriptlet Doc/write context.
Relocated the ORM-like model identifier, XOR-in-literal observation, 256-entry
array fill, PHP temporary-file creation and parseUri identity to their supported
subjects, updating consumers. Renamed the generic Reverse token to remove the
false CLR requirement. Retired SHA256 proximity-only stage-locator inference;
the Netstruct consumer now requires its concrete GitHub URL leg. Axios data
access now binds the promise callback parameter to its data member, rather
than labeling every req/res.data field as an HTTP response.

Eleven positive and near-miss controls are in cases.json; run:
python3 testdata/taxonomy/source-library-offerbundle-review/check.py
All eleven passed. Original samples were scanned with atomscan and cleave facts;
all three were rescanned after edits. The archive has zero hostile/suspicious
YAML findings after correction. Bootstrap has zero hostile/suspicious findings.
Native executables were not run. Initial and final scan/facts reports, IFPS
disassembly, retrieved configuration and downloaded dependency bytes are in:
/usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-c608bc37/scratch/triage-bad/
